reply: Pushing back on the restore ask: removing tracked measurement artifacts is the deliberate core of this PR, not an accident. Measurement outputs and `out/facts*.json` are now generated by a measurement run and published via the bundle flow (`bench publish`, documented in the RELEASING.md this same PR updates, consistent with the already-published et-v0.9.5 bundle), so `perf/pins.py` reads `out/facts.json` after that run produces it rather than from a stale tracked copy. Keeping release facts in git would defeat the artifacts-via-bundle model; the missing-file ergonomics point is separately valid and tracked from the CodeRabbit thread on `perf/pins.py`.

The gitlink removal is intentional, not a hand-moved pin: editor checkouts now live in the unmanaged repos-style layout, and the pin record moves to the generated `out/facts.json` (`ver.*` keys), with AGENTS.md's rule that pins only move via `build/update_editors.sh` during a release unchanged. The docsplus harness itself (`harness/docsplus/roundtrip.ts`) is updated in this PR for the new checkout layout, and a fresh checkout creates the editor checkout before the trial runs, so we do not read the deletion as breaking the docsplus lane by design. If a concrete fresh-checkout failure of `_run_docsplus` shows up, we will fix the path handling as a follow-up — but not by restoring a tracked gitlink.

Valid finding: with `--outdir` set to the input's own directory, soffice's expected output path is the input path, so `produced.is_file()` is vacuously true and `produced.replace(outdocx)` can move unconverted input bytes into place as the C02 output. We will convert into a dedicated per-sample subdirectory so the produced file can never be the input, and re-check the affected LibreOffice rows. The same defect was filed independently by CodeRabbit on this file.

Correct: the cold arm's clock starts after `goto(domcontentloaded)` has already returned while the warm reload arm starts before navigation, so the paired C03 delta carries navigation time on one side only and biases `attribute_delta` toward the `document_parse` label. We will measure both arms from navigation start (matching the puppeteer path) and re-derive the affected C03 pairs. CodeRabbit filed the same boundary mismatch in its warm_cold_browser.mjs thread.

Agreed — both bare `# noqa: E402` directives on the `reportgen` and `assert_markdown_no_editor_speed_ranking` imports get an inline justification stating that ROOT must be on `sys.path` before these imports.

Agreed — every template read in the rendering flow, including the one inside the anti-ranking guard, gets an explicit `encoding="utf-8"`; the reports contain non-ASCII text and must not depend on the platform locale default.

Agreed — the plan still describes the pre-implementation static `PINS`/`EVIDENCE` design, which contradicts the shipped `load_editor_pins` that reads pins from `out/facts.json`. We will update the plan to describe the facts-driven pin resolution and stop prescribing specific hash values, so an agent following the plan cannot produce code that diverges from the module.

Agreed — the plan's interface line for the fresh-process criteria set is stale against the implementation's `_FRESH` set; we will sync the listed IDs (adding C07–C09, C11, C12, C14, C22, C23) so the plan is self-consistent.

Agreed — the machine-specific absolute module ID makes the `vi.mock` silently inactive on any other checkout, so the real `WorkerManager` loads and fails under jsdom. A relative specifier resolves against the test file the same way imports do and works everywhere; we will apply it.

Agreed — collapsing `VITEST_DOCX_OUTPUT` to a basename under `TRIAL_ROOT/out/canvas` writes samples outside the runner's temp directory, leaves `last_outdocx` pointing at a nonexistent file, and silently deprives the canvas C02 correctness check of its output text. We will use the full resolved path as `OUT_DOCX`, keep the current defaults when the variable is unset, and make the write step create the output file's own directory.

Agreed — literal hashes embedded in the `EVIDENCE` notes go stale at the first pin move and can then contradict `out/facts.json`. We will phrase the notes pin-agnostically (or derive the pin reference via `pin_label(...)` at call time) so capability evidence always matches the recorded release pins.

Agreed — `trial_or_refusal` currently works only because every non-`supported` override happens to be a refusal outcome; a new value like `partial` would surface as a misleading refusal-outcome error. We will validate the capability state explicitly and reject unrecognized states with a clear message.

Agreed — the guard as written passes 'twice as fast as', bare 'faster than', and '5 times faster than', which weakens a design-rule guard. We will widen `_SPEED_RANK` to cover the multiplier, 'times', and 'as fast as' forms (case-insensitive) and add tests for each phrasing.

Agreed — we will document in the docstring that omitted `cache_state`/`host_class` are silently defaulted to `process_cold_fs_warm`/`ci_coarse`, and that the conservative `ci_coarse` default blocks publication.

Agreed — a NaN sample makes `sorted` order undefined and silently corrupts the percentile, MAD and CI. We will reject non-numeric and non-finite samples at the entry of `summarize` before any statistics are computed.

Agreed — putting all paragraphs into one `<w:t>` with raw newlines produces a single-paragraph document, so the measured bytes do not match the declared `fixture_paragraph_count` shape. We will emit one `<w:p>` per paragraph with escaped text in its own `<w:t>` and assert the parsed paragraph count in the fixture tests.

Agreed — we will add a module docstring to `perf/fixtures/oracles.py` stating that `grapheme_spans` and `backspace_grapheme` support only their hard-coded fixture strings and are not general segmentation functions.

Agreed — C01 advertises `input_ready` and `deferred_quiescence` in its `marks` field but `classify_mark` rejects both with 'unknown mark'. We will add both to `_MARKS` under the correct layer categories rather than weakening the unknown-mark error.

Agreed — the `(raw + 4) // 8 * 8` tie behavior is an assumption, not a verified rule: the spec only states 8 ms granularity and the current tests do not separate half-up from ceiling. We will add an exact-tie test and document the confirmed rule beside `rounded_duration_ms`, changing the implementation only if the evidence demands it.

Agreed — the final check can only fire when a report has no boundary sample at all, so naming `compile_and_instantiate` there misleads. We will reword it to state that no WASM boundary sample exists for the report.

Agreed — a raw `FileNotFoundError` from the cached `editor_pins()` gives no path forward. We will wrap it to name the missing `out/facts.json` path and the step that produces it (a measurement run, per this PR's artifacts-via-bundle model) before any runner starts work.

Agreed — `page.waitForFunction` accepts the expression string directly, so the `eval` wrapper (and Biome's `noGlobalEval` error) goes away; we will keep the errors-are-false semantics by writing the ready expressions defensively.

Agreed — on `micro-paragraphs` many editors have no container with more than 200 px of overflow, so the probe can return rAF overhead as a C10 scroll sample and the runner records it as `measured`. We will make the probe report whether a scroll happened and fail loudly when nothing did, instead of writing a fabricated C10 trial.

Agreed — each module-level `# noqa: E402` gets an inline justification for the `sys.path` bootstrap (or the pattern moves to a Ruff `per-file-ignores` entry for `perf/runner/*.py`), and the directive on the function-local import at line 87 is removed since E402 does not apply there.

Agreed — same rule as the other bootstrap runners: the 14 bare `# noqa: E402` directives each get a justification, or the whole pattern moves to a Ruff `per-file-ignores` entry for `perf/runner/*.py`.
Agreed — we will justify the module-level `# noqa: E402` directives inline (or consolidate them into a `per-file-ignores` entry) and remove the spurious one on the function-local import at line 981.

Agreed — `proc.kill()` on a `start_new_session=True` process leaves the Vite child holding the port (and `--strictPort` then fails the next run for that editor), while an unread `stderr=PIPE` can block the server mid-probe. We will reap the whole process group on timeout and route stderr to a temp file that is read on failure.

Agreed — if `_run_browser_probe` raises, the except path records the error but never stops the Plate dev server, which then outlives the script holding port 5208. We will move `_stop_server(proc)` into a `finally` that runs on both success and failure.
Agreed — same fix as the C10 probe: pass `readyJs` directly as the first argument to `page.waitForFunction` and drop the `eval` wrapper Biome flags as `noGlobalEval`, preserving the existing timeout.

Agreed — we will type-check `stats["n"]` (rejecting bools and non-ints) before any conversion or comparison, so malformed input surfaces as the documented `ValueError("summary_stats n")` instead of an uncaught `TypeError`.
Agreed — both honesty tests error when `soffice` is not on PATH; we will add `@unittest.skipUnless(shutil.which("soffice"), ...)` so they stay active wherever LibreOffice is installed.

Agreed — the coverage-matrix path must be anchored to the repository root (the `REPO`-anchored pattern `test_unblocked_browser_harness.py` already uses) so the suite passes when run from `perf/` or any other working directory.

Agreed — a clean checkout has no `perf/out/unblocked_2026_11_07b/attempts`, so this honesty test fails without a prior measurement run. We will ship a minimal fixture under the tests tree and point the test at it, skipping only when neither fixture nor generated output is present.

Agreed — `startsWith(DIST)` without a trailing separator admits sibling paths such as `dist-other`, and `decodeURIComponent` throws a 500 on malformed escapes like `%E0%A4%A`. We will switch the DIST and WASM checks to `path.relative` containment and pass malformed URIs to `next()`; the 127.0.0.1 binding limits exposure but the fix is cheap and exact.

Agreed — with `outdir` equal to the input directory, `produced.is_file()` is vacuously true (including when soffice exits 0 because another instance holds the user profile), so C02 can record a no-op as `measured` and the I01 text check reads the original input. We will write the conversion into an isolated per-sample directory; this is the same defect tracked from the gitar-bot thread on `_run_libreoffice`.

Agreed — the paired C03 row cites `c03_cold_attempt_ref` as `warm_path`, so the warm median's cited evidence is the cold attempt file and the `reload_samples` series is never persisted. We will write a `warm_steady` C03 attempt from `reload_samples` and reference it, keeping the one-C03-per-editor behavior of `assert_no_duplicate_c02_c03_in_dir` consistent with the fix.

Agreed — cold `modelReadyMs` starts after `goto` resolves while the warm `documentReloadSameContextMs` span starts before navigation, so the paired C03 delta contains navigation time on one side only and skews toward 'warm is slower' with a `document_parse` attribution. We will measure both arms from navigation start and update `attribute_delta`'s probe-median assumptions and tests accordingly — same defect as the gitar-bot C03 thread on this file.
